purpose: PINN and DeepONet pricers for two-stock Heston basket options with every Heston parameter and both correlations as inputs, each built as a ladder: every level adds one technique to the configuration below it, and every level is scored on the same validation contracts. Levels follow the four-stock ladders (4d/) with the one-stock Heston variance boundary (heston/).
selection_rule: Within each family the level with the lowest validation score is selected. Score = mean over price and every Greek of RMSE / RMS(reference) on the validation contracts drawn from the protocol's training domain. A level within 1% of the best score yields to the earlier level. The references are simulations, so each summary also records the noise floor RMS(reference standard error) / RMS(reference) per quantity; a level is not better than another by less than that floor.

computational_domain.note: Spatial extent of the PDE problem in z = log basket forward moneyness, the forward shares s_i >= share_floor and each variance v_i in [0, v_hi], like a grid solver's far boundaries. The Heston parameters, the correlations and the maturity cap are the protocol's training domain; tau starts at 0 because the PDE starts at the payoff. Initial variances of the domain lie in [0.01, 0.36]; v_hi = 1.5 leaves room for the variance to wander, with c_v = 0 imposed there from P4 and D4 on.

labels.note: Training labels and anchors: one shared Sobol net of 1,024 conditional QE paths with 32 time steps for every contract (src/neural/reference.py reference_labels), seeded by seeds.label_normals. Price and the first and second derivatives in the log forwards.

evaluation.note: Monitor and validation references: heston_estimate per contract (8 replicates of 1,024 Sobol paths, QE step 1/32, every quantity with its standard error), contract k seeded by seeds.evaluation_normals + k for the validation panel and + 100000 + k for the monitor and short panels. Built in worker processes.
